exposure: Mode of delivery (Caesarean section vs. natural delivery)
cohort: Newborns from two independent Copenhagen Prospective Studies on Asthma in Childhood cohorts (COPSAC2010, n=677 and COPSAC2000, n=387)
finding: Caesarean section was associated with distinct newborn metabolomic profiles, characterized by lower abundance of tryptophan, bile acid and phenylalanine metabolites, and an increased risk of asthma at school age.
mod_finding: The metabolic profile associated with caesarean section was linked to altered gut microbiome composition, suggesting a potential influence of delivery mode on gut colonization and subsequent asthma risk.
